prompt.alinti: There's a new cloud technique that's been blowing people's minds this week, and it comes straight from the team that built Cloud. It's called a verification loop, and it fixes the most annoying part of using Cloud. You know when you ask Cloud to build something, and it says it's finished, then you try it, and it's actually broken? Basically, a verification loop makes Cloud test its own work before it ever tells you it's done. So instead of babysitting it, Cloud tries out what it built itself.
So if you ask for a new button on your website, it clicks that button itself and actually takes a screenshot to prove it worked.
When something's broken, Cloud fixes it, tests it again, and keeps going until everything actually works.
The first time, Cloud figures out how to test your project and saves those steps so it runs the exact same test every time after.
I put the full setup in a guide comment verified.
